title: A Hymn for the Choir
premise: Casper Fairweather has spent years as a night hospice nurse, comforted by a private ritual: the dying count backwards from ten, and when they reach zero, they go. But when Casper's home sleep-recording app captures a second voice answering questions no one asked aloud — questions about doors, names, and debts — the counting begins in their own apartment. The voice belongs to something that was invited in decades ago by Casper's late grandmother, whose hospice was never really a hospice. As the night stretches toward sunrise, Casper must gather the ragged found family of former patients and coworkers who owe their lives to that old house, uncover what bargain bought their survival, and decide whether to pay the debt themselves or let it fall on someone who can't refuse.
about_author: Yara Vasquez is a former overnight caregiver who writes horror drawn from the strange intimacies of end-of-life work. She lives in a coastal town where she keeps her own doors counted, purely as a hobby.

chapters.title: Ten
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. A routine shift at Marigold House hospice; Mr. Aldous counts backwards from ten in his sleep and dies at zero, peaceful, smiling. Casper's ritual of counting doors and checking lights establishes their careful, controlled world. Emotional beat: tender unease — comfort built on a superstition Casper half-believes.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. At home, Casper reviews their sleep-tracking audio out of boredom and hears a second voice answering questions Casper never asked: 'How many doors?' 'Three.' 'Who let you in?' Silence. Casper tells themself it's a glitch. Emotional beat: denial curdling into dread as the voice says Casper's childhood nickname.

chapters.title: Doors Counted
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper obsessively audits the apartment — three doors, exactly as the voice said, though there should be four including the closet. The closet door won't stay shut. Coworker Dev notices Casper's exhaustion and covers a shift for them. Emotional beat: isolation beginning to crack; the first hint of found family.

chapters.title: What Nana Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Sorting through grandmother Ruth's estate boxes, Casper finds patient ledgers from Ruth's private hospice — every name crossed out at death, every ledger page ending in a backwards count, and one page listing 'payments received.' Emotional beat: grief complicated by suspicion; the woman who raised Casper may have been something else.

chapters.title: Nine
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The recording now captures the second voice counting down from nine each night, one number lower per night. Casper's neighbor Mrs. Okafor, a former patient of Ruth's, goes pale when told — she remembers the counting from 1987. Emotional beat: the horror stops being private; someone else believes.

chapters.title: The Survivors
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Mrs. Okafor gathers the others: Dev, whose brother died at Marigold House; Imogen, a former patient cured of terminal cancer at Ruth's; and quiet Tomas, who never speaks of his time there. Six people, all alive when they shouldn't be. Emotional beat: fragile solidarity — a family assembled by debt.

chapters.title: Payments Received
chapters.summary: POV: Imogen. Flashback chapter through Imogen's memory of Ruth's hospice: the singing, the backwards counts, the night Ruth stood in the hallway bargaining with something in the walls. Imogen woke up healthy and never asked why. Emotional beat: guilt — survival purchased without consent.

chapters.title: Eight
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The count reaches eight; the closet door is now warm. Casper dreams of a long corridor lined with numbered doors and wakes with dirt under their fingernails. Dev stays the night uninvited, refusing to leave Casper alone. Emotional beat: fear tempered by loyalty; the family tightens.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: POV: Mrs. Okafor. She lays out what she knows: the thing honors invitations above all, keeps accounts to the letter, and can be bargained with but not refused once named. Ruth's rule — never thank it, never answer its questions — is written in the ledger margins. Emotional beat: grim clarity; knowledge as both weapon and trap.

chapters.title: Seven
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The voice asks its first direct question of Casper: 'Are you the heir?' Casper says nothing, but the recording captures their sleeping breath answering yes. Something has been signed. Emotional beat: betrayal by one's own body; the trap closing.

chapters.title: Tomas Breaks
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas. He confesses he was Ruth's last payment — a child given over in 1999, returned hollow, his voice taken until adulthood. He came back tonight because the thing called him by name an hour ago. Emotional beat: raw grief and rage; the cost of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Six
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The group attempts to un-invite it: salt, renunciations, burning the ledgers. The fire refuses to catch on Ruth's pages. In the smoke, Casper sees the corridor again — and this time a door stands open at the far end. Emotional beat: defiance meeting futility; desperation sets in.

chapters.title: The Bargain Replayed
chapters.summary: POV: Imogen. The group reconstructs Ruth's original contract from ledger fragments: Ruth traded years of her patients' deaths — taken slowly, painlessly — in exchange for the cures. The debt wasn't paid; it was deferred, and it passes to the heir. Emotional beat: horrified understanding of Nana's love as a kind of theft.

chapters.title: Five
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. With five nights left, the group debates offering someone else. Imogen volunteers; Tomas argues it should be him, finishing what was started. Casper refuses to let either pay for Ruth's choice. Emotional beat: the theme sharpened — power corrupts even the ones trying to be good.

chapters.title: Sunrise Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Dev. Dev proposes exploiting the letter of the law: the thing keeps accounts, so give it an account it cannot collect — a payment made of everything at once, or nothing properly owed. They plan to confront it in the corridor before the count reaches zero. Emotional beat: hope with teeth; the found family becomes a strategy.

chapters.title: Four
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Preparation night. Casper writes letters they may not survive sending, learns the ledger's final page is blank except for one line: 'Heir's signature pending.' The voice whispers thanks for the first time — which Ruth's rules say means it considers the deal closed. Emotional beat: quiet terror and tenderness braided together.

chapters.title: Three
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The apartment begins rearranging itself; the corridor bleeds into the hallway. Mrs. Okafor is briefly taken behind a door and returned aged ten years. The group realizes the house will pick its own payment if they don't choose. Emotional beat: panic; control slipping entirely away.

chapters.title: Two
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper enters the corridor deliberately, carrying the blank ledger page, and finds the thing wearing Ruth's voice. It offers the same deal Ruth took: Casper's patients' deaths, stretched thin, in exchange for everyone walking free. Emotional beat: the temptation of power offered gently — corruption knocking politely.

chapters.title: One
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper nearly signs — imagines saving Dev's dying mother, easing every future patient — then understands this is how Ruth began. Instead Casper offers the only honest payment: themself, fully, no deferral, no heirs. The thing hesitates; it has never been offered a clean account. Emotional beat: climax of moral clarity against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The count reaches zero. Casper walks through the open door — and the found family breaks the terms: they follow, answering the thing's questions in unison, muddying the account until the debt is owed to six people at once and collapses under its own arithmetic. The corridor burns clean this time. Emotional beat: triumphant chaos; love as a loophole.

chapters.title: After the Counting
chapters.summary: POV: Imogen. Weeks later: the recordings are silent, the closet door opens onto coats. Casper survived, changed — they no longer hear the dying count, and grieves the loss like a limb. The survivors keep meeting Sundays, a family with no debt holding it together for the first time. Emotional beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: A Hymn for the Choir
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Closing chapter: at Marigold House, a new dying patient hums an unfamiliar hymn, and Casper chooses to sing along rather than count. Power, they've learned, is what you agree to carry for others. Final image: six voices in a small room, doors counted, lights on, sunrise coming. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, vigilance kept as devotion.
